A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPDS-ADMM work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E support comparison, including the expanded experiments in v4.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original sparse-PCA experiments comparing objective values against runtime on eight data matrices.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original sparse-PCA experiments, including convergence curves across regularization and initial-penalty settings in Figures 1–17.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same penalty and smoothing schedules, proximal block updates and relaxed multiplier update. The parameter-selection formulas are unchanged apart from notation; revised experimental parameter choices do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sparse PCA using Gaussian random matrices, MNIST, TDT2 and sector data. The additional parameter combinations and changed MNIST feature counts retain the same data sources and task.

E2.justification: The main and appendix experiments consistently retain SubGrad, SPGM and RADMM as comparators. Revisions to the literature comparison in Table 1 do not add experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes sigma from 1.5 to approximately 1.618 and xi from 0.9 to 0.5. Appendix E expands fixed beta0=50ρ experiments into beta0/ρ={10,50,100,500}, adds ρ=1000, and changes MNIST feature counts from 500 to 780. The plots now report common 20-second windows instead of dataset-dependent windows.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 expands comparisons at three regularization values and one initial-penalty multiplier into a joint four-by-four parameter study. This directly examines sensitivity to the initial penalty and reveals poor behavior at small penalties and slower convergence in some large-penalty settings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional curves retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 reports replacement convergence curves and sixteen parameter combinations versus three in v3. For example, Figure 3 shows SPGM reaching much lower objectives than IPDS-ADMM at ρ=10 and beta0=10ρ, exposing a failure case absent from v3's settings. Changed parameters and MNIST dimensions prevent interpreting the replacement curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 Definition 4.17 and Theorem 4.18 use summed squared residuals and p in (0,1/2); v4 Definition 4.14 and Theorem 4.15 use unsquared residuals and state bounds for p in (0,1). Appendix D.13 substantially reworks the complexity derivation while retaining O(ε^-3) at p=1/3. The rewritten Lemma D.1 also introduces coefficients proportional to 1−1/sigma without absolute values, which become negative in the allowed under-relaxed case.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same headline claims: IPDS-ADMM under one-block continuity, convergence for bijective and surjective operator cases, O(ε^-3) critical-point complexity, and empirical effectiveness on sparse PCA.

C2.justification: Remark 4.16 newly explains p=1/3 as balancing the two rate terms. Appendix E.3 singles out beta0=50ρ and 100ρ as favorable settings, but its broad 'consistently outperforms' interpretation does not explain the failures visible at smaller penalties.

D1.justification: Code-access directions change from supplemental material to the author's research webpage, without a direct URL. v4 explicitly reports theta1=1.01 and theta2=0.60 where v3 reports only theta=1.01. MATLAB, hardware, data preparation and orthogonality-projection details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Franca et al. (2018), Lin et al. (2022b) and Yuan (2024, 2025), removes several inertial-method citations, and revises RADMM's stated scope and Table 1's assumption descriptions. Remark 3.7 replaces the assertion that Lemmas 3.4–3.5 are novel with their derivation through standard convex analysis.

P1.justification: The main section and appendix organization remains intact. v4 consolidates related-work discussion and several lemma/proof pairs, renames Section 3 subsections, edits explanatory prose, and adds acknowledgments and a conference header. Most narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Experimental presentation expands from three figures to seventeen, including sixteen appendix parameter combinations and a new mapping table. Figure 1 repeats Figure 8's setting. Curves, time axes, MNIST labels and captions are revised; Table 1 is relocated and highlights nonsmoothness assumptions in color.

improvement.justification: The expanded penalty study provides useful sensitivity and failure evidence absent from v3. However, the rewritten complexity proof introduces coefficients c3 and c6 proportional to 1−1/sigma without absolute values in Lemma D.1; these are negative for the advertised sigma<1 case, whereas v3 uses squared factors. The empirical benefits coexist with a new gap in the central theoretical argument, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
